subject: Vulnerability Management: Consolidated evidence and patch SLA language for RFP
messages:
From: Elena Soto <elena.soto@helix-fin.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@helix-fin.com
Date: Tue, 25 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: Vulnerability management evidence for RFP - Helix Financial

Hi Vivek / Monica,

Thanks again for the demo last week. As part of our procurement review for Helix Financial's platform refresh, we need a consolidated vulnerability-management evidence bundle to evaluate against our security baseline. Specifically we need: 

- SAST/DAST program summary (tools, cadence, ownership)
- Recent penetration test executive summary and remediation status (last 12 months)
- Patch SLA commitments and historical compliance metrics (30/60/90 windows)
- SBOM export for your core inference service and third-party components
- Any compensating controls (WAF, runtime protections, segmentation)

Can you share a single packet and a short cover note describing the items above by EOD Friday (May 28)? If you expect any items to be redacted, please call that out.

Best,
Elena
Elena Soto
Director, Vendor Risk Management
Helix Financial

P.S. If you prefer we can accept a secure Drive link or DocuSign-hosted evidence delivery.
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Soto <elena.soto@helix-fin.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 25 May 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: Vulnerability management evidence for RFP - Helix Financial

Elena — thanks for the clear list. We'll compile a consolidated packet and call out any items that require redaction. Initial plan:

- VM_Evidence_Packet_v1.pdf: SAST/DAST program + owner matrix + cadence
- RedLabs_Pentest_Summary_202704.pdf: executive summary + remediation status (open/closed/mitigated)
- SBOM_export_202705.csv: component inventory for inference service runtime
- VM_Appendix_PatchSLAs.docx: proposed SLA language + historical 30/60/90 compliance table

Soojin will pull the SBOM and pen-test artifacts; Monica will confirm the SLA numbers and historical metrics. We will deliver the Drive link and a short cover email by EOD Friday (May 28). If you need any evidence earlier, we can expedite the pen-test executive summary.

Thanks,
Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Product, Redwood Inference
V: (415) 555-0162

Date: Wed, 26 May 2027 10:18:00 -07:00
Subject: RedLabs — Executive summary and remediation notes (April 2027 engagement)

Hi team,

Attaching the executive summary from our April engagement. Highlights:

- Scope: inference runtime components + web admin UI + CI/CD pipeline interfaces
- Findings: 7 medium, 2 high (both related to misconfigured TLS settings on internal staging), 0 critical
- Remediation: 6 medium closed, 2 medium mitigated with compensating controls, high items resolved and verified on 2027-04-21

We included a short proof-of-fix checklist for each verified item. Note: we redacted IP-level scan logs from the public summary; full logs are available under NDA if needed.

Regards,
Marcus Reed
Principal Security Consultant | RedLabs Secure
pen-test@redlabs.io

Attachment stubs: RedLabs_Pentest_Summary_202704.pdf (pdf)
From: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 27 May 2027 09:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Internal: Patch SLA wording and compliance metrics (please review)

Team — drafting the appendix for Helix. A few decisions to confirm before we finalize: 

1) SLA tiers: propose we commit to: 
   - Critical: patch within 30 days (security hotfixes; customer-impacting exploitation)
   - High: patch within 60 days (validated exploits, active scanner detection)
   - Medium/Low: patch schedule based on risk prioritization, target 90 days for nonurgent

2) Historical compliance: I pulled the last 12 months from our patch tracker: Critical: 100% within 30 days (6/6), High: 92% within 60 days (23/25), Medium: 87% within 90 days (48/55). I will include a small table in VM_Appendix_PatchSLAs.docx.

3) Compensating controls: for packages that require longer lead time (3rd party kernel updates, vendor-managed drivers) we will call out runtime mitigations (network segmentation, ephemeral credentials, ACLs).

Ben — can you add a short note on how we instrument and audit patching (triggers, ticketing, automated rollout pipelines)? Soojin — please confirm SBOM extract path and whether we should include signature hashes or only package names/versions.

If no objections, I'll stitch this into the packet and upload by Friday morning.

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Manager, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
